options: Sector ETFs trend upward for 5 days after a strong move
Short-term sector overreaction mean-reverts over roughly 5 trading days, more strongly when the VIX is elevated
Sector returns are unrelated to volatility under any condition
Individual stocks mean-revert faster than sector ETFs
questions.explain: The working hypothesis is that short-term sector overreaction mean-reverts over about 5 trading days, and that this effect is stronger in high-VIX regimes than in calm ones.

questions.q: Why does SR-5 test sector ETFs instead of individual stocks?
options: Individual stocks don't have enough historical data
Sector ETFs are more liquid, diversify away company-specific noise, and form a clean, manageable cross-section
Sector ETFs can't be shorted
Individual stocks don't trade on the same exchange
questions.explain: Single stocks are dominated by idiosyncratic, company-specific noise. Sector ETFs diversify that away, are highly liquid, and form a clean 11-name cross-section.

questions.q: What does 'cross-sectional' mean in the context of this signal?
options: Comparing a sector's current return to its own history only
Comparing each sector's return to the other sectors on the same day
Comparing the strategy's return to a risk-free rate
Comparing daily returns across different decades
questions.explain: A cross-sectional signal ranks each sector against the other sectors on the same date, rather than measuring an asset only against its own past.

questions.q: What is the null hypothesis (H₀) for SR-5?
options: Past 5-day sector returns are strongly predictive of forward 5-day returns in the same direction
Past 5-day sector returns have no relationship to forward 5-day returns — any apparent pattern is noise
The VIX has no effect on any trading strategy
Sector ETFs always outperform SPY
questions.explain: The null hypothesis states there is no real relationship between past and forward 5-day returns — observed patterns would just be statistical noise.

questions.q: What does 'regime conditioning' mean in this project?
options: Only trading during market holidays
Allowing the strength of an effect to depend on a separate state variable, here the VIX level and term structure
Switching between stocks and bonds based on interest rates
Ignoring volatility entirely when sizing positions
questions.explain: Regime conditioning means the reversal signal's strength is allowed to vary depending on a separate variable — here, the VIX regime — rather than assuming a constant effect through time.
